content.content: Read the dependent's ignore artifact and the packaged set the dependent commits to against the packaged set the prerequisite records, in both directions. The prerequisite's set is the runtime payload exactly — out/extension.js, media/webview.html, src/styles/*.css, src/webview/main.js, and from node_modules only @vscode/codicons/dist/codicon.css with the codicon.ttf it loads — plus the packaging metadata the packager force-includes, the manifest and the README, which the ignore artifact can neither add nor keep out. The dependent's exclude/keep list is then read file by file against the six prerequisites it names, and each of their files takes the place its own record gives it. The check suite and the runner configuration kuvpymsu owns, tests/integration/srlrwowp.test.ts and .vscode-test.mjs, and those nrwunqtx owns, tests/unit/zswmtqst-conformance.test.ts and vitest.config.ts, are development-only and must be excluded; any rule that excludes them passes — one reaching the suite's directory, as the artifact's tests/** does, or one naming the configuration outright, as .vscode-test.mjs and vitest.config.ts are named — and a rule set that leaves any of them admitted fails. The licence rnqkxwsu records, LICENSE, is a repository document outside the packaged set, so it must be excluded by name, and because the packager takes its licence asset only from a file the ignore rules already admitted, that exclusion is what keeps the licence out rather than an inert line. The repository ignore file rxqsupwm records, .gitignore, is likewise excluded by name. The TypeScript sources the shell and the page composition are written in — src/extension.ts, src/panel.ts and src/webview/main.ts — are built into out/extension.js and never shipped, so the artifact's src/**/*.ts rule must reach every one of them. The page tpztomkv's composition serves, media/webview.html, is payload, so no exclusion rule may match it: the artifact says so both by carrying no rule that reaches the path and by naming it in its kept list, and either alone is read, so a kept list that omits the page while no rule excludes it is a divergence to name rather than to accept. The manifest package.json that srlrwowp owns holds the one place the artifact cannot decide: it is force-included metadata, so the artifact neither lists it nor could exclude it, and a rule that tried to would diverge in the stricter direction without effect. LOOSER: fail when the packaged set the dependent commits to, or the filtering its artifact produces, admits a file outside that set — a TypeScript source, test, design note, node document, schema, build configuration, licence text, repository ignore file, or a dependency the payload does not name, including any file of the six prerequisites that the set keeps out. STRICTER: fail when the dependent's packaged set denies a file the prerequisite names, including the manifest, the README, or the page the composition serves. The check does not require README.md to exist in the repository: the manifest and the README are metadata by virtue of what the packager includes, and the dependent is judged on stating and enforcing that the runtime payload and the packaging metadata are distinct, not on the file being present. Fail naming the file and the direction it diverges in.
content.rationale: The dependent's artifact is the packaging ignore file, a tool-checkable artifact (code layer), while the packaged set is stated in prose (natural layer), so the edge sits in the matrix's natural-to-code cell and takes the fidelity form: the prose cannot itself decide, file by file, what the packager will carry, so the ignore artifact is where conformance is settled, and the artifact and the packaged set the dependent commits to must enforce the prose exactly, no stricter and no looser, with each divergence named. Fidelity is a review, not a runnable listing: the refined prerequisite adds packaging metadata the packager includes independently of the ignore artifact, and a packager listing cannot show force-included metadata that is absent from the tree, so a file-list test would fail for the file's absence rather than for the dependent's claim and would need a file this decision does not own. Reading the artifact's effect and the packaged set the dependent states against the prerequisite in both directions keeps the check independent of the dependent's wording — any rewrite that commits to the same packaged set passes — while a set that drops the manifest or README, or admits an extra file, fails naming it. The prose is unenforced until the dependent commits to and enforces the runtime/metadata distinction this check reads. Amended for the six prerequisites the dependent's exclude/keep list names: the place a file holds in the packaged set is not settled by its class alone, so the earlier criterion, which read only the class-level rules against vqultolm's set, could pass an artifact that drew the right classes and still kept out the page tpztomkv's composition serves or admitted the runner configuration that brings no extension host. The criterion therefore reads the artifact against each file those prerequisites own — kuvpymsu's extension-host suite and its runner configuration, nrwunqtx's unit suite and vitest configuration, rnqkxwsu's LICENSE, rxqsupwm's .gitignore, srlrwowp's manifest and shell sources, tpztomkv's page and page entry point — in the direction each record fixes and with the rule or its absence named. A form chosen edge by edge from the layers would put these six edges in the code-to-code test cell or the fidelity cell depending on whether the prerequisite carries suites and configurations or prose, but the dependent side is one artifact read once and the question per file is a direction rather than a behaviour: what the artifact says about a path is read from the artifact itself with the deciding rule named, so one review answers all six edges and no harness adds anything the reading does not already say. Nothing here re-decides the other uses of the same files: how the repository ignore file draws the packaged set's line for git is pqzmtzov's edge, and which dependency the packager resolves into the vsix is the gate on srlrwowp's dependency declaration.
